on_off.help: On or off: on or 1, off or 0.

framing.help: The reply framing: on for JSON-RPC, off for text.

address.help: A memory address in hex, 0x optional, at most eight digits.

block.help: A block length in bytes, 1 to 64.

hex_bytes.help: Bytes as hex pairs, spaces allowed between pairs.

mask.help: A mask in hex, no prefix; its digit count is the width: 2, 4 or 8.

help.help: The board's commands, each name mapped to its one-line help; help <command> answers that command's line.

json.help: Set the reply framing, on for JSON-RPC or off for text; bare json reads it.
json.long_help: json off switches the board to text replies: every reply after it is text, not JSON, until json on, or any request line starting with {, switches back.  The config sends json on when the MCP server connects.

led.help: Turn the RGB LED on, a dim white, or off; bare led reads it.  The reply is the state, on or off.

led_rgb.help: Set the RGB LED's red, green and blue levels, each 0 to 255; bare led_rgb reads them.  The reply is the levels, [red, green, blue].

typed_args.name: red
typed_args.help: Red level, 0 to 255; give all three levels or none.

temp.help: Read the chip's temperature sensor, in whole degrees Celsius, as a number.

id.help: The chip's unique ID in hex, its factory MAC address.

MEM.R.help: Read memory at an address: rows of hex bytes, then OK.  Prefer /mem.read, which checks the address first.
MEM.R.long_help: The board reads whatever address it is given.  One the chip cannot reach resets it, and reading a peripheral register can change it (a FIFO pops).  /mem.read names registers from the device file and refuses sweeps of peripheral space.

MEM.W.help: Write bytes to memory at an address, then OK.  Prefer /mem.write, which checks the address first.
MEM.W.long_help: The board writes whatever address it is given; one the chip cannot reach resets it.

MEM.M.help: Masked write with interrupts off, word = (word & and) | or; the reply is the word before, then OK.
MEM.M.long_help: The masks have the same digit count, which sets the width (2, 4 or 8 for a byte, a half or a word), and the address is aligned to it.  /mem.write X.bit and /mem.or use it.

MEM.INFO.help: The memory interface: block limit, address width, byte order, and whether MEM.M is there.
